chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him), and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on them all, narrated from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Sa'id ibn Janah, from Abu Yahya al-Hadda', from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) looked at al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said, 'O 'Abrat (tear) of every believer!' He (al-Husayn) said, 'Am I, O my father?' He (the Commander of the Believers) said, 'Yes, O my son!'
ai.seo_question: What does the title 'Abrat Kulli Mu'min' (Tear of every believer) signify regarding Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam Ali (a.s.) bestows the title 'Abrahah' (Tear of Weeping) upon Husayn (a.s.), signifying that his martyrdom serves as a perpetual source of spiritual catharsis and emotional connection for the faithful. This designation underscores the theological concept of *Shafa'ah* (intercession) through grief, where the believer's tears for Husayn are not merely expressions of sorrow but acts of devotion that purify the heart and affirm the enduring legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt.
